title: Verb + -ing or to ... 1 (remember, regret etc.)
subtitle: remember doing / remember to do
summary: Choose between -ing and to ... after remember, regret and go on, where the two forms have different meanings, and after begin/start/continue, where they do not.

lesson.heading: Two groups of verbs
lesson.note: Some verbs can be followed by -ing or to ... with a difference of meaning: remember, regret, go on.

left.label: I remember doing something
left.text: = I did it and now I remember this. You remember doing something after you have done it.
examples: I know I locked the door. I clearly **remember locking** it.
He could **remember driving** along the road just before the accident, but he couldn't remember the accident itself.

right.label: I remembered to do something
right.text: = I remembered that I had to do it, so I did it. You remember to do something before you do it.
examples: I **remembered to lock** the door, but I forgot to shut the windows.
**Remember to buy** some bananas. (= Don't forget to buy them)

left.label: I regret doing something
left.text: = I did it and now I am sorry about it.
examples: I now **regret saying** what I said. I shouldn't have said it.
Do you **regret not going** to college?

right.label: I regret to say / to tell you / to inform you
right.text: = I am sorry that I have to say (formal).
examples: (from a formal letter) I **regret to say** that we are unable to accept your offer.

left.label: go on doing something
examples: The president paused for a moment and then **went on talking**.
We need to change. We can't **go on living** like this.

right.label: go on to do something
examples: After discussing the economy, the president **went on to talk** about foreign policy.

lesson.heading: begin / start / continue / intend / bother
lesson.text: We use these verbs with -ing or to ... with **no difference of meaning**. But normally we do not use -ing after -ing.
remember/forget + to = the task is still ahead (Remember to lock it). remember/forget + -ing = looking back at something you did (I remember locking it).

exercises.explanation: enjoy is always followed by -ing: enjoy driving.

exercises.prompt: I can't afford ___ away. I don't have enough money.
exercises.explanation: afford is followed by to ...: can't afford to go away.

exercises.prompt: The driver of one of the cars admitted ___ the accident.
exercises.explanation: admit is followed by -ing: admitted causing the accident.

exercises.prompt: Sarah doesn't know about the meeting. I forgot ___ her.
exercises.explanation: forget to do = you did not do it because you forgot: I forgot to tell her.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with its meaning.

pairs.right: I locked it, and now I remember this.

pairs.left: I remembered to lock the door.
pairs.right: I knew I had to lock it, so I did.
I said it and now I am sorry about it.

pairs.left: I regret to say we cannot accept your offer.
pairs.right: I am sorry that I have to say this.
He continued doing the same thing.

pairs.left: He went on to talk about foreign policy.

exercises.prompt: Tom cried on his first day at school, but he can't remember this now. He doesn't remember ___ on his first day at school.
exercises.explanation: remember + -ing looks back at something that happened: doesn't remember crying.

exercises.prompt: Once Tom was bitten by a dog, but he can't remember this. He doesn't remember ___ by a dog.
exercises.explanation: remember + -ing for a past event; the passive -ing form is being bitten.

exercises.prompt: When you see Steve, remember ___ hello to him from me.
exercises.explanation: remember to do = don't forget to do it (the action is still ahead): remember to say hello.

exercises.prompt: The course I did wasn't very good, but I don't regret ___ it.
exercises.explanation: regret doing = I did it and (do not) feel sorry about it: don't regret doing it.

exercises.prompt: Ben became assistant manager after two years, and a few years later he went on ___ manager of the company.
exercises.explanation: go on to do = do something new (a new job): went on to become manager.
It's starting to rain. Normally we do not use -ing after -ing.
